He then watched a meeting between Galen and Director [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] as the later arrived in a shuttle with a squad of [[death trooper]]s. Missing several opportunities to take him out,<ref name="Rogue One" /> Cassian hesitated to fire<ref name="From the Shadows" /> and realized there was more to the situation than what met the eye, ultimately deciding there must be another way as<ref name="Rogue One" /> he lowered his blaster. His change of heart either came from his murder of Tivik finally catching up to his conscious or his adventure with Erso, and meeting with Gerrera, having changed his way of thinking.<ref name="From the Shadows" />

[[File:Cassian-rescues-Jyn.png|thumb|right|330px|Andor rescues Erso after her father's death.]]
However, the Rebellion's [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Blue Squadron]] came and attacked the facility. The squadron had been launched by Draven when he lost contact with Cassian following their crash. Rebel X-wings bombed the platform, killing Galen in the process. He made his way to the platform and rescued Jyn, who had ascended the platform to find her father herself, and the group left on a stolen [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|''Zeta''-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle]] and returned to Yavin 4.<ref name="Rogue One" />

====Back on Yavin 4====
{{Quote|They were never gonna believe you.''"<br />"''I appreciate the support.''"<br />"''But I do. I believe you. We'd like to volunteer.|Andor and Jyn Erso, following the Rebellion's initial refusal to go to Scarif|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
As they proceeded back to base, alerting Alliance Command that they were in a stolen shuttle, an angry and sorrowful Jyn confronted Cassian, telling him that she had figured out that he was planning on killing her father.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Although Cassian was defensive<ref name="From the Shadows" /> and reminded her that he even had a chance to pull the trigger and did not, Jyn retorted that he may as well have, since he ended up being killed by Alliance forces.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Revealing the buried anguish that fueled his fight against the Empire,<ref name="From the Shadows" /> Cassian quickly grew angry at her accusations and reminded her that he had been in the fight for much longer than she had and that she was not the only one that had lost everything doing so.<ref name="Rogue One" />

[[File:DeathStarBriefing-SWBC38.png|thumb|left|320px|Cassian Andor (center) during the meeting with Alliance High Command]]
Jyn tried to convince the alliance to attack [[Scarif]] in order to retrieve the plans to the Death Star, but many of the council members were despairing, lamenting how they had already lost the war and talking about disbanding. Mon Mothma told Jyn that they could not proceed with her proposed attack without more support, so Jyn stormed away from the meeting. However, knowing this would happen, Cassian began assembling a [[Rogue One|squad]] of Rebel assassins, mercenaries, and soldiers to go and fight on Scarif to retrieve the plans, going directly against the wishes of High Command. Meeting Jyn in the hangar, Andor confessed that neither he nor the rebels he gathered could live with themselves if they turned back now and said that they were willing to go with her to fight. Baze, Chirrut, Bodhi, and K-2SO also joined them. Together, they took the [[SW-0608|stolen Imperial shuttle]] and left for Scarif, with Rook piloting. When an air traffic control officer contacted Rook and asked what he was doing flying the ship, which had not been authorized for takeoff, Andor told him that he had to lie, and although Rook temporarily stumbled, he eventually said that their squad, "Rogue One," was lifting off.<ref name="Rogue One" />

===Sacrifice on Scarif===
{{Quote|Make ten men feel like a hundred.|Cassian Andor to Rogue One|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
[[File:ScarifInfiltration.png|thumb|right|330px|Cassian, Jyn, and K-2SO sneak into the security complex]]
Rook was able to use Imperial clearance codes to pass the [[Shield Gate]] that protected the planet and steered the shuttle to [[Landing Platform Nine]]. There, Andor gave command of the troops to [[Sergeant]] [[Ruescott Melshi]], instructing them to place explosives around the landing sites that surrounded the [[Citadel Tower]]. Meanwhile, after ambushing a trio of Imperials who came aboard to inspect their ship, Andor joined Jyn in stealing their uniforms, dressing as an Imperial officer, and infiltrating the facility with K-2SO.<ref name="Rogue One" />

Inside, K-2 accessed another droid to find a map to reach the plans. When they neared the area where the plans were kept, Andor was contacted by Melshi, who told him that the soldiers outside were ready to go. Andor gave the command to blow the charges, and a widespread firefight began outside as a full [[Scarif Deployment|garrison]] on Imperial troops were deployed to fight the invaders. Meanwhile, as Andor and Jyn attempted to retrieve the plans, a group of stormtroopers arrived and discovered that K-2, who was left outside to watch, was an enemy. K-2 sealed Andor and Jyn inside to protect them and sacrificed himself in a fight against several stormtroopers.<ref name="Rogue One" />

[[File:Jyn-cassiandeath.png|thumb|left|330px|Cassian's and Jyn's death]]
As troopers began to attempt to breach the doors, Andor and Jyn decided to retrieve the plans by hand instead of using the mechanism and began to climb to reach them. When Krennic made his way inside, he shot Andor, who fell as Jyn continued to climb upwards to escape through a hatch. Andor survived and limped his way after Jyn, who had ascended to the top of the citadel to transmit the plans to the rebel fleet that had arrived over Scarif. After Jyn avoided a TIE, she was about to transmit the plans when Krennic arrived again. However, before he could kill Jyn, Andor saved her and shot Krennic, wounding him and escaping with Jyn.<ref name="Rogue One" />

Seeking to ensure the plans would fall into the hands of those who could change the tide of the struggle against the Empire,<ref name="From the Shadows" /> Andor and Jyn beamed the plans to the fleet and went back to the beach where many of their rebel comrades lay dead. As they knelt on the sand, they watched as the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] fired at Scarif and destroyed the base. Cassian told Jyn that her father would be very proud of her. The two then accepted their fate and shared a final embrace before they were killed in the resulting blast.<ref name="Rogue One" />

===Legacy===
[[File:Exds.png|thumb|right|275px|Andor's efforts helped lead to the destruction of the Death Star.]]
With his bravery having helped to turn the tide of the conflict between the Empire and the Rebellion, Andor became a hero to the Rebel Alliance. Although the path towards victory was littered with the emotional costs soldiers like Andor had paid by compromising on their morals, he had helped change the course of the Rebellion<ref name="From the Shadows" /> and history as a whole.<ref name="Episode IV">{{Film|IV}}</ref> After Rogue One transmitted the plans to their fellow rebels,<ref name="Rogue One" /> the intel was used to eventually destroy the Death Star at the [[Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="Episode IV" />, ironically the station he had indirectly helped create during his time on [[Narkina 5 Imperial Prison Complex|Narkina Five.]]<ref name="Episode 12" /> As the Galactic Civil War wore on, [[Luke Skywalker]], the pilot who had destroyed the Death Star, named a new starfighter group [[Rogue Squadron]] in honor of Andor's team.<ref name="Star Wars 52">[[Star Wars (2015) 52|''Star Wars'' (2015) 52]]</ref>

After the Battle of Yavin, a rebel group known as the [[Shrikes]] were [[Ambush on Taanab|ambushed]] on [[Taanab]] by agents of the ISB. The Alliance captured a transmission from [[Hutt Space]] from the sole survivor, [[Caluan Ematt]]. In a memo to Mothma, Draven wished Andor were alive, as he would have been Draven's first pick to extract Ematt and bring him to safety for his knowledge and expertise of the [[Hutt]] underworld.<ref name="Rebel Files" />

==Personality and traits==
===Overview===
{{Quote|Does he look like a killer?''"<br />"''No. He has the face of a friend.|Chirrut Îmwe and Baze Malbus|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
A good rebel agent who held dark secrets,<ref name="Helmet Collection 56" /> Andor was a human male standing at 1.78 [[meter]]s tall,<ref name="Visual Guide" /> with [[Color|brown-black]] hair and brown eyes.<ref name="Rogue One" /> He held a reputation for having striking good looks, which he used to lure in the unsuspecting during his service as a Rebel spy.<ref name="Galactic Survival Skills">''[[Star Wars: How Not to Get Eaten by Ewoks and Other Galactic Survival Skills]]''</ref>

===Younger days===
[[File:CassianAndorFugitive-Portfolio.png|thumb|Cassian changed his appearance before joining the [[Aldhani rebel infiltration team|infiltration team]].]]
As a young man, Andor kept his origins close to his chest, officially denoting that he hailed from the planet Fest instead of revealing the true nature of his childhood on Kenari. However, he did trust some close friends and romantic partners with the truth, including [[Bix Caleen]]. He did not tell many, but he also did not keep track of everyone that he told.<ref name="Episode 2" /> Although he had needed to leave her behind<ref name="217 Kassa" /> years prior,<ref name="Episode 1" /> Andor also never forgot his sister Kerri<ref name="217 Kassa" /> and actively searched for her. He was prone to owing various individuals money, at one point being in debt to [[Nurchi]] and [[Brasso]], the latter of whom he was more keen to pay back due to being good friends with the man.<ref name="Episode 1" />

He also had a reputation of being something of a womanizer. When trying to explain away a mysterious injury to Caleen, the latter wondered if it may have been caused by a jealous husband.<ref name="Episode 1" /> When Andor's mother [[Maarva Carassi Andor|Maarva]] was trying to figure out who knew that Andor was born on Kenari, she stated that she was worried about "all his women," naming some of them before admitting that there were some names that even she did not know.<ref name="Episode 2" /> [[Arvel Skeen]] was quick to inform Andor that their fellow [[Aldhani rebel infiltration team]] member [[Cinta Kaz]] was already "sharing a [[blanket]]."<ref name="Episode 5">{{Andor|The Axe Forgets}}</ref> Andor eventually developed into<ref name="20 Highlights">{{SW|url=news/swca-2022-20-highlights-from-lucasfilms-studio-showcase|text=SWCA 2022: 20 Highlights from Lucasfilm's Studio Showcase}}</ref><ref name="212 Launchpad">{{InsiderCite|212|Launchpad}}</ref> a selfless man, which set him apart from other, more extreme rebels who blurred the same lines as him.<ref name="From the Shadows" />

===Rebel agent===
{{Quote|If I die tonight, was it worth it? You've done this before. You must have thought about it.''"<br />"''This makes it worth it. This. Right now. Being with you. Being here at the moment you step into the circle. Look at me. You made this decision long ago. The Empire cannot win. You'll never feel right unless you're doing what you can to stop them. You're coming home to yourself. You've become more than your fear. Let that protect you.|Niya and Cassian Andor|<ref name="OYL" />}}
As a Rebel, Andor was a committed, steady, practical, and by-the-book intelligence officer with a fair amount of combat experience,<ref name="Rogue One" /> but that experience grew from missions that sometimes blurred the line between what was morally wrong or right. Despite his selflessness,<ref name="From the Shadows" /> he was cold and distant to others.<ref name="Helmet Collection 56" /> Andor often kept quiet and reserved, a trait he had acquired due to his experience in war. Although fighting on the side of the Rebel Alliance, he'd been hardened by war to the point that he did not hesitate to commit morally questionable acts when necessary.<ref name="Rogue One" /> During those days of the early rebel movement, he relied on the excuse that he was following orders to justify what he had done.<ref name="From the Shadows" />

[[File:CassianAndorFull-Fathead.png|thumb|left|200px|Cassian Andor during the Rebellion]]
Although he displayed some degree of remorse and regret after some of his actions—such as his choice to execute Tivik during the mission to the Ring of Kafrene—it was never enough to convince him to seek redemption until his adventure with Jyn Erso.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Nevertheless, he was more morally conflicted than fellow insurgent Saw Gerrera, who also went to great lengths to uncover intelligence on topics, particularly weapons, that threatened the Rebels.<ref name="From the Shadows" /> In a briefing to Mothma, General Draven described Andor as "one of the most capable agents within Rebel Intelligence," with the ability to handle a wide range of missions, from reconnaissance to [[assassin]]ation and [[Saboteur|sabotage]]. Draven also said that Andor was capable of analyzing intelligence and acting on that intelligence without the need to contact superiors. Draven indicated that, since Andor worked for the rebellion since childhood, that the Alliance was like his family and that his loyalty was unwavering. Mothma, however, worried about the terrible things Andor and other Rebel agents were asked to do in the name of the Rebellion.<ref name="Rebel Dossier">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Rebel Dossier]]''</ref> Indeed, many of the missions he carried out for the Alliance were morally questionable.<ref name="From the Shadows" /> Mothma wondered if the command was doing enough to help agents like Andor to cope with the psychological damage inflicted by their actions.<ref name="Rebel Dossier" />

Comprising on their morals in the name of victory was dreadful for the emotional health of Rebels like Andor. In truth, Andor had been driven to the extremes he carried out by the anguish he carried inside him. Having lost everything in his life, Andor was able to hold back thinking about his morally questionable actions<ref name="From the Shadows" /> until his time with Erso.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Whether it was due to killing Tivik or a change in his outlook due to the adventure he had with Erso,<ref name="From the Shadows" /> he disobeyed orders to kill Galen Erso<ref name="Rogue One" /> before revealing his internal anguish by arguing with Jyn; she compared him to a stormtrooper for following orders he thought were wrong,<ref name="From the Shadows" /> which made him burst out in anger because of all he had done in the name of rebellion.<ref name="Rogue One" /> In the end, Andor's selflessness<ref name="From the Shadows" /> and regret for his past actions<ref name="Rogue One" /> led to him joining the ragtag Rogue One mission.<ref name="From the Shadows" /> Meeting Erso and joining that mission helped Andor remember why he became a Rebel agent in the first place.<ref name="Helmet Collection 56" /> Paying the ultimate sacrifice he could in the apogee of his selfless devotion to the Rebel Alliance<ref name="From the Shadows" /> and wanting to bring a new hope to the galaxy, Andor willingly gave his life<ref name="Helmet Collection 56" /> to ensure the Death Star plans were given to those who could use them to win the war.<ref name="From the Shadows" />

==Skills and abilities==
{{Quote|He can pilot. He can shoot. He can lie. He speaks Alarin, Myo, Nari. He's got steady nerves and he's not afraid to kill.|Luthen Rael, about Cassian Andor|audio=CassianLanguages-Luthen-Aldhani.flac|<ref name="Aldhani">{{Andor|Aldhani (episode)}}</ref>}}
Andor found that gathering intelligence required more than spying alone. He was an expert in espionage, [[Saboteur|sabotage]], and assassination throughout his missions.<ref name="From the Shadows" /> Andor was a committed soldier and fighter, rebelling against various regimes over the course of his life. Although sometimes he questioned his actions, he accepted that he did what had to be done in the name of a good cause. He was prepared to double-cross allies to get the job done. On one occasion, he killed his informant Tivik instead of risking letting him be captured by Imperial forces.<ref name="Rogue One" />

Andor was often an unassuming man that his opponents would underestimate. After killing two [[Tac-Corpo|Corpos]] on [[Morlana One]], the [[Consolidated Holdings of Preox-Morlana Corporation|Preox-Morlana]] sent a squad after him, with [[Linus Mosk]] warning the group not to underestimate Andor.<ref name="Episode 2" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|His weapon ''was'' in the sniper configuration.|K-2SO on Cassian Andor's A280-CFE blaster|<ref name="Rogue One" />}}
[[File:AndorMW20BryarPistol-Reckoning.jpg|thumb|200px|Cassian wielding his adoptive father's MW20.]]
Prior to joining the Rebellion, Andor wielded an [[MW-20 Bryar pistol]], which was wielded by his adopted father [[Clem Andor]] years earlier.<ref name="Episode 3" /> Andor carried [[B1-NA blaster pistol|Karn's blaster]] for a time. During the preparation for a [[Aldhani heist|mission]] on [[Aldhani]], [[Arvel Skeen]] became suspicious of Andor after seeing the corporate-issue blaster and questioned Andor as to whom it belonged to.<ref name="Episode 5" /> After the mission, Andor stashed the weapon away in a hidden box on [[Niamos]], where it was left after he was arrested and detained in the [[Narkina 5 Imperial Prison Complex]].<ref name="Announcement">{{Andor|Announcement}}</ref> When Andor later returned to the planet with [[Ruescott Melshi]] after their [[Narkina 5 prison escape|escape]] from [[Narkina 5]], he retrieved the box and handed the blaster off to Melshi before the two parted ways.<ref name="Episode 11" />

[[File:CassianAndor-Databank.png|thumb|left|210px|Andor with his A280-CFE, set in the pistol configuration]]As a member of the Rebellion, Andor wore a brown [[Corellian]]-cut [[field jacket]] that depicted his military rank and also held a personal identifier transponder that concealed a [[suicide pill]]. He also wore brown military fatigues. On Jedha and Eadu he used a blue-colored coat with fur lining. Andor owned a [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft]] called the LMTR-20.<ref name="Rogue One" />

He carried a canvas bag over one shoulder on the Ring of Kafrene and a [[backpack]] on Jedha. Andor carried an [[Jyn Erso's blaster|A-180 blaster]] before Erso stole it.<ref name="Rogue One" /> Due to his years of law-bending, Andor had honed his escapology skills, and he carried a compact [[security kit]] hidden inside one of his boots.<ref name="Visual Guide" />

[[File:AndorRingOfKafrene-R1.png|thumb|right|250px|Cassian's concealed blaster.]]
Cassian was capable with a variety of blasters. He primarily wielded a [[BlasTech Industries|BlasTech]] [[A280-CFE convertible heavy blaster pistol|A280-CFE blaster]]—a versatile, modular [[heavy blaster pistol]] that could be reconfigured into an [[assault rifle]] or [[sniper rifle]] by adding a [[barrel]] and [[stock]] attachments, which he carried in a thigh [[holster]]. On the Ring of Kafrene, Andor killed Tivik and a pair of stormtroopers with a concealed blaster pistol of unidentified model. He used the same weapon to dispatch Krennic during the Battle of Scarif.<ref name="Rogue One" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Conception and portrayal===
{{Quote|I think what's remarkable is the sacrifice that Cassian Andor makes for the galaxy.''"<br />"''I know what he represents. This is the story about the people. It's a story that has the most to do with us. It's about what we can do, it's about the power we have.|[[Kathleen Kennedy]] and Diego Luna reflect on Cassian Andor's story|<ref name="20 Highlights" />}}
Cassian Jeron Andor, portrayed by [[Diego Luna]], is a character created and developed for the [[2016]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|film]] ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]''. Luna's casting in the film was first announced on [[August 15]], [[2015]]. At this time, the first photo of the character was released,<ref name="Rogue One Cast">{{SW|url=news/rogue-one-the-daring-mission-has-begun-cast-and-crew-announced|text=''Rogue One''—The Daring Mission Has Begun: Cast and Crew Announced}}</ref> and the first footage of the character was shown in the ''Rogue One'' teaser trailer on [[April 7]], 2016.<ref name="Teaser">{{SWYouTube|2BDyeARyIkw|Rogue One: A Star Wars Story Trailer Tease}}</ref>

Luna spoke with his natural [[Wikipedia:Mexicans|Mexican]] accent while playing Andor.<ref name="Accent">{{WebCite|url=http://ew.com/movies/2017/01/04/rogue-one-diego-luna-fan-story-diversity|text=Diego Luna 'got emotional' over fan story about diversity in ''Rogue One''|author=Derschowitz, Jessica|date=2017-01-04|archivedate=20191109032330}}</ref> When Luna jumped to the tower<ref name="Tricky lines">{{YouTube|video=0q25e6uuFwA|text="Star Wars means so much!" Diego Luna and the Andor cast on auditions, tricky lines and falling over|channel=@bbcradio1|name=BBC Radio 1}}</ref> in the Scarif vault,<ref name="Rogue One" /> he broke his rib but did not notice it. He did not tell anyone about his injury.<ref name="Tricky lines" /> After ''Rogue One''{{'s}} release, Luna shared a story from a fan who took her Mexican father to see the film because of his accent, which he said made him emotional.<ref name="Accent" />

The younger Cassian Andor as seen in the episode "[[Kassa]]" was played by [[Antonio Viña]].<ref name="Episode 1" />

===''Andor'' and further development===
{{Quote|There's so much that this series answers, that Rogue One just questions. For me, ''Rogue One'' is very much about an event, and now we're going to get the chance to actually understand and get to know [Cassian Andor] — who he is, what pain he carries. What are his fears? What is his real motivation? It's all going to be answered here.|Diego Luna discussing ''Andor''|<ref name="This Story Matters">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/diego-luna-andor-star-wars-rogue-one|text=Diego Luna on returning to Star Wars with Andor: 'This story matters'|author=Coggan, Devan|date=2022-08-25|archivedate=20220825150430}}</ref>}}
[[File:Andor_Promotional_Banner.png|thumb|left|280px|Concept art of Cassian Andor on Ferrix by Vincent Jenkins]]
By [[2018]], [[Lucasfilm]] has begun developing a television series set before ''Rogue One'' which starred Andor and K-2SO. They would be similar to the film characters [[Wikipedia:Butch Cassidy|Butch Cassidy]] and the [[Wikipedia:Sundance Kid|Sundance Kid]], and they would storm the Citadel. After viewing the script sent by Lucasfilm,<ref name="Real People">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How 'Andor' Became the First 'Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: 'I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}}</ref> ''Rogue One'' writer<ref name="Rogue One" /> [[Tony Gilroy]] thought the material was fine but hard to sustain over a long run. He then wrote a forensic manifesto explaining why the idea would not work and what Lucasfilm should do instead.<ref name="Real People" /> Gilroy explained that the show should have a large hole that Andor climbs out of over the course of five years. Gilroy added that Andor's journey should not involve escapades with K-2SO because it could get repetitive.<ref name="Gilroy podcast">{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2022/09/andor-tony-gilroy-podcast-interview-1235127456|text='Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy On Building "Complex" 'Star Wars' Series With Budget Bigger Than 'Michael Clayton' – Crew Call Podcast|author=D'Alessandro, Anthony|date=2022-09-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline Hollywood'']]|archivedate=20220926215710}}</ref> Gilroy's idea became the ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' television series,<ref name="Real People" /> which was called "The Education of Cassian Andor" during early development.<ref name="Education">{{SW|url=news/tony-gilroy-andor-interview|text="The Education of Cassian Andor": Creator Tony Gilroy Explores the Nuance of ''Andor''}}</ref> The show would explore Andor's backstory, revealing how he changed from a nihilist into a selfless martyr. Gilroy wanted the [[Andor Season 1|first season]] to explain why Andor sacrificed himself in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Rebellion televised">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/star-wars-cover-the-rebellion-will-be-televised|text=''Star Wars:'' The Rebellion Will Be Televised|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-17|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220517110251}}</ref> When Gilroy was conceptualizing Andor's larger story arc, he started to map out a narrative journey for Andor that would feel compelling and complete. This included showing Andor at a low point in his life at a time when the Empire was gaining power across the galaxy.<ref name="ProductionBrief 2">{{Getty|url=thewaltdisneystudios/allaccess#!asset/gppr5wpqgb4t74974f8s|text=ANDOR Production Brief V3 FINAL 8-04-22}}</ref> Gilroy used Andor's story to depict the intertwining lives of common people as they orbit around the formation of the Rebel Alliance.<ref name="Real People" />

To create a 24-episode series spanning five years, the show's directors worked in blocks of three episodes with Season One having four blocks.<ref name="Five year">{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/andor-tony-gilroy-explains-star-wars-rogue-one-prequel-structure-exclusive|text=Andor: Tony Gilroy Explains Star Wars' Rogue One Prequel Series' Epic Five-Year Structure — Exclusive Image|author=Travis, Ben|date=2022-07-04|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20220704132220}}</ref> Gilroy realized that maintaining the show's scope for four more seasons would be overwhelming, so he and executive producer [[Sanne Wohlenberg]] decided to use the same structure used in Season One.<ref name="Real People" /> For [[Andor Season 2|Season Two]], Gilroy and the crew decided to use each block to represent a year, which Gilroy found to be very exciting from a narrative point of view.<ref name="Five year" />

[[File:CassianAndorLuthenRaelConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of Cassian Andor and Luthen Rael escaping Ferrix by Chester Carr and Luke Hull]]
Gilroy was drawn to the idea of a story spanning Andor's childhood origin and a five-year history that takes him to a revolution.<ref name="Potent Moment">{{SW|url=news/andor-launch-interview-gilroy-and-cast|text="A Potent Moment in History": Insights from Tony Gilroy and the ''Andor'' Cast}}</ref> The show had Andor stop pretending he is not affected by the Empire and choose who he is going to be. Gilroy used Andor's line about being in this fight since he was six years old as a jumping off point to create Kenari.<ref name="Education" /> Andor's murder of<ref name="Murderous">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/tv/andor-diego-luna-premiere-interview|text=Diego Luna weighs in on Cassian's murderous moment on ''Andor''|author=Ross, Dalton|date=2022-09-22|archivedate=20220922134718}}</ref> Kravas Drezzer and Verlo Skiff in the episode "[[Kassa (episode)|Kassa]]"<ref name="Episode 1" /> was meant to show that he is a survivor in an oppressive galaxy with no sense of justice. Andor's decision to spare Syril Karn was meant to show that he learns from his mistakes.<ref name="Murderous" /> Giloy wanted to have Melshi in the show, so he figured that the Narkina 5 prison was a great place to show where and how they met.<ref name="Easter eggs">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-tony-gilroy-talks-luthen-rael-monologue-easter-eggs-1235258961|text='Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy Talks Luthen Rael's Future and Being Surprised by Certain Easter Eggs|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221109220924}}</ref> During the writers' room in [[November]], [[2019]], Gilroy told the writers he was interested in seeing Andor escape during a prison sequence.<ref name="Vision to life">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-beau-willimon-sanne-wohlenberg-interview|text='Andor's EP Sanne Wohlenberg and Writer Beau Willimon on Bringing Tony Gilroy's Vision to Life|author=Lovitt, Maggie|date=2022-11-10|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20221110211930}}</ref> In an early iteration of the story, Andor and the prisoners would steal the guards' boots to escape the prison<ref name="Breaks down">{{SW|url=news/tony-gilroy-andor-season-1-interview|text=Tony Gilroy Breaks Down ''Andor'' Season 1}}</ref> on Narkina 5.<ref name="Episode 10" /> Writer [[Beau Willimon]] said the goal of the prison episodes was to make Andor feel the Empire's oppression in a serious, sustained, and inescapable way. He viewed Andor as a recruiter for Kino Loy in a similar way to how Luthen Rael recruited Andor.<ref name="Grown-up">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1091309/andor-writer-and-executive-producer-on-making-a-grown-up-star-wars-show-exclusive-interview|text=Andor Writer And Executive Producer On Making A Grown-Up Star Wars Show [Exclusive Interview]|author=Mathai, Jeremy|date=2022-11-09|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20221109190722}}</ref> Concept art depicting Andor was created by concept artists [[Vincent Jenkins]], [[Chester Carr]], [[Peter McKinstry]].<ref name="Andor Concept Art Gallery">{{SW|url=andor-concept-art-gallery|text=Concept Art Gallery | Andor}}</ref> and [[Luke Hull]].<ref name="Period drama">{{WebCite|url=https://www.theverge.com/23445550/star-wars-andor-production-costume-design-interview|text=Andor's designers approached it like a Star Wars period drama|author=Webster, Andrew|work=[[Wikipedia:The Verge|''The Verge'']]|archivedate=20221109181234}}</ref>

In mid-2019, Gilroy called Diego Luna and told him the full plan for an Andor-focused story. Luna was glad that Gilroy's proposal included details that resonated personally with him<ref name="Rebellion televised" /> and he was convinced by Gilroy's ground-level approach.<ref name="Real People" /> At the end of the call, Luna agreed to reprise his role in the series.<ref name="Rebellion televised" /> He then talked about returning for two or three years before shooting started.<ref name="Challenge Rogue">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-diego-luna-talks-star-wars-return-season-2-1235209806|text=Diego Luna Says 'Andor' Is Going to Challenge What You Think You Know About 'Rogue One'|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-09-01|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20220922232520}}</ref> Luna was excited to explore the darker side of Andor's psyche, as well as to show the nuance and complexity of a younger version of the character.<ref name="ProductionBrief 2" /> To prepare for reprising his role, Luna imagined aspects of Andor's history that never made it into ''Rogue One'', and he used that as background to bring the character to life. He and Gilroy discussed this as the scripts came together, helping to personalize Andor for the actor. Luna thought about people who are forced to run due to outside pressures, but decide to stop and make a stand.<ref name="All wrong">{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/andor-star-wars-series-diego-luna|text='Andor' Star Wars Series: "What You Know Is Really All Wrong"|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/5PVTM}}</ref>

Costume designer [[Michael Wilkinson]] was tasked with making Andor someone who can disappear by hiding in his clothes but still be compelling, have "some swagger," and be something the audience is drawn to. Wilkinson decided that the arc of Andor's costumes would begin with him hiding in his clothes due to being a mess-up. As the series progressed, Andor shed his layers a little bit and his silhouette became more tailored with longer lines, and his shoulders became square. This was intended to show Andor is subtly becoming the character he is in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="Wardrobe">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/andor-interview-michael-wilkinson-star-wars|text='Andor's Costume Designer on Creating Cassian's Wardrobe and Returning for Season 2|author=Lovitt, Maggie|date=2022-11-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20221114190034}}</ref> The Aldhani rebels' disguises were made using natural fabrics. Wilkinson made the costumes very dark, textural, and organic.<ref name="Wilkinson interview">{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-galaxy-designer-michael-wilkinson-defines-the-look-of-andor-s-costumes|text=Dressing the Galaxy: Designer Michael Wilkinson Defines the Look of <i>Andor</i>'s Costumes}}</ref>

Production began in late [[November]] of [[2020]].<ref name="New Lucasfilm">{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}}</ref> Scenes on Ferrix were filmed in an intricate set in [[Wikipedia:Marlow, Buckinghamshire|Little Marlow]], [[Wikipedia:Buckinghamshire|Buckinghamshire]].<ref name="ProductionBrief 2" /> According to Tony Gilroy, everything on Ferrix was filmed first.<ref name="Good day">{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-features/andor-season-2-post-credits-scene-tony-gilroy-1235268962|text='Andor' Creator Tony Gilroy Talks Luthen's Good Day, That Post-Credit Scene and Season Two|author=Davids, Brian|date=2022-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:The Hollywood Reporter|''The Hollywood Reporter'']]|archivedate=20221123185515}}</ref> As Luna spent more time on set, he started to enjoy the process more and fall in love with his character,<ref name="This Story Matters" /> and he did not enjoy playing the role until the third or fourth day. He felt that his costume was either too big or too small.<ref name="Challenge Rogue" /> The actor managed to embody a rash and more impulsive Andor with a younger mindset.<ref name="ProductionBrief 2" /> Luna aimed to let audiences understand his character and explain how six-year-old Andor got wrapped up in a rebellion. He said that the trick is in telling a story that people can connect with and explaining how Andor got to where he was in ''Rogue One''.<ref name="This Story Matters" /> Luna found it very important to understand that the show depicts a childish version of Andor who is unaware of the consequences of his actions.<ref name="Murderous" />

===Continuity===
====Legends precedents====
Andor has multiple equivalent characters in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity. 2016's ''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide]]'' mentions that Andor used the codename "Aach" as a senatorial contact on [[Darkknell]].<ref name="Visual Guide" /> The [[Aach|codename]] originated in the [[1999]] Legends short story "[[Interlude at Darkknell]]" by [[Timothy Zahn]] and [[Michael A. Stackpole]], where it was used by a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] agent of [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] who met with Senator [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] and informed him about Organa's discovery of the construction of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="Interlude at Darkknell">{{StoryCite|story=Interlude at Darkknell|book=Tales from the New Republic}}</ref> The [[2008]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement ''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]'' mentioned that a [[Unidentified bodyguard|bodyguard]] had [[Escape from Coruscant (Mon Mothma)|escorted]] [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]]<ref name="The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> into hiding from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> a role that Cassian would play in the 2025 ''Andor'' episode "[[Welcome to the Rebellion]]."<ref name="Welcome" />

====Discrepancies====
=====Fest and age=====
{{Quote|We have always said Fest. Every doc I've ever submitted has always said you were born on Fest.|Maarva Andor, to Cassian Andor|<ref name="Episode 2" />}}
''Star Wars: Rogue One: The Ultimate Visual Guide'' states that Cassian Andor was born on Fest, 26 years before the events of ''Rogue One'',<ref name="Visual Guide" /> which corresponds to [[26 BBY]].<ref name="Atlas" /> This was repeated in later sources.<ref name="ROSM">''[[Star Wars: Rogue One: Secret Mission]]''</ref><ref name="AEYNTKUE">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]''</ref><ref name="Helmet Collection 56" /><ref name="USWNE">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref><ref name="Heroes of">{{EncyclopediaCite|The Heroes of Rogue One}}</ref><ref name="SWCEUAEE">''[[Star Wars: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> However, with the release of ''Andor'' in 2022, the titular character's place of birth was confirmed to be Kenari.<ref name="Episode 1" /> Thereafter, Andor's updated [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry on [[StarWars.com]] states that the character was nine years old when he was taken off Kenari,<ref name="Cassian DB" /> while the StarWars.com Episode Guide for the "[[Reckoning (episode)|Reckoning]]" episode of ''Andor'', released on [[September 21]], 2022, states that the Confederacy of Independent Systems had yet to be formed and the Clone Wars was yet to be fought at the time of the character's departure from Kenari.<ref name="Ep3EG" /> Since previous sources establish that the Confederacy was formed in either [[24 BBY]] or 22 BBY and the Clone Wars started in 22 BBY,<ref name="CISdate">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' establishes that the [[Raxus Address]] and the following informal forming of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] occurred two [[Standard year|years]] before the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], which marked the start of the [[Clone Wars]] in {{Film|II}}, the events of which took place in [[22 BBY]], according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''. Therefore, the Confederacy was informally founded in [[24 BBY]]. ''Attack of the Clones'' also depicts the formal founding of the Confederacy.</ref> this article assumes that Cassian Andor must have been born no later than nine years before 24 BBY, or [[33 BBY]], making the previously stated birth year of 26 BBY impossible. Indeed, the later reference book ''[[Star Wars: Dawn of Rebellion: The Visual Guide]]'' helped narrow down Andor's birthdate to 33 BBY.<ref name="birthyear" />

=====Meeting K-2SO=====
[[File:AndorKaytooWecacoe-CassianK2SOSpecial1.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Cassian and K-2SO on Wecacoe in the ''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'']]
''Andor'' Season 2 provides its own explanation of how Andor met the droid K-2SO<ref name="Welcome" /> that disregards the story told in the one-shot comic [[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]].<ref name="Cassian and & K-2SO">[[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]]</ref> Series creator [[Tony Gilroy]] was aware of the comic, however chose not to adapt the events, instead choosing to write a new origin for K2.<ref name="Interview">{{YouTube|video=4Hk3w9W0ZjA|text=Tony Gilroy talks ANDOR, STAR WARS, BOURNE, MICHAEL CLAYTON I Happy Sad Confused|channel=JoshHorowitz|name=Josh Horowitz}}</ref> In that comic, Cassian proposed a mission to Draven to recover Imperial protocols on [[Wecacoe]]. Draven suggested that Cassian take the [[twin]]s [[Kertas]] and [[Rismor]], who were renowned for their skill in gathering Imperial intelligence. However, the twins did not speak much, as they communicated via smell. The team expected a limited Imperial presence due to the fact that Wecacoe was a backwater planet, but upon arriving, they found the facility guarded by swarms of [[KX-series security droid]]s and [[stormtrooper]]s, Cassian imagined [[Alliance High Command]] ordering him to turn back, but, determined not to end up empty-handed, decided to proceed. The team slipped into a sewage pipe and entered the [[Storage facility 47|storage facility]] to find an abandoned Imperial [[cruiser]]. Unfortunately, they were spotted entering the tunnels and stormtroopers began investigating the area using surveillance cameras.<ref name="Cassian and & K-2SO" />

While they were hurriedly searching for data, Cassian looked for another way out. Suddenly, an alarm rang out and the team was forced to flee. Since there were too many troops along the perimeter, Cassian decided to distract one of the security droids, [[K-2SO]], and then shut him down. The droid pinned him, but then the twins shut him down and removed his memory. K-2SO escorted the spies to their ship, but they were soon intercepted by stormtroopers. When they arrived at their ship, they found it surrounded by troopers. Both of the twins ran off, telling him that K-2 had all the info they needed. Suddenly, their ship exploded. Cassian realized that he had to get rid of the base programming to have the droid as an ally, and deleted the last memories. The pair than ran to a ship and hijacked it. Then, Cassian took the droid back to ship to learn the new Imperial security protocols.<ref name="Cassian and & K-2SO" />
